headline: Harden session and admin cookies with __Host- / __Secure- name prefixes
summary: The session, login, and admin cookies now carry the browser-enforced `__Host-` / `__Secure-` name prefixes when served over HTTPS. These prefixes bind a cookie to a secure, same-origin context — a browser only accepts a `__Host-` cookie that was set with `Secure`, `Path=/`, and no `Domain` attribute — which closes off cookie-injection and session-fixation paths from a related origin or a non-secure context. The secure-versus-plain decision follows the forwarded request protocol, so a deployment behind a TLS-terminating proxy (the production setup) gets the hardened prefixes while local development and tests over HTTP keep the bare names and keep working. Returning visitors are not signed out by the upgrade: the cookie reader resolves both the prefixed and the legacy name during the transition.

items.title: `__Host-` on the session and login cookies
items.body: Over HTTPS the storefront session and login cookies are issued as `__Host-shop_sid` and `__Host-shop_auth` with `Secure`, `Path=/`, and no `Domain` — the attribute set a browser requires before it will store a `__Host-` cookie, so the session cookie can no longer be planted or overwritten by a related origin or a non-secure context.

items.title: `__Secure-` on the admin cookie
items.body: The admin session cookie is scoped to `Path=/admin`, so it takes the `__Secure-` prefix (which requires `Secure`) rather than `__Host-` (which mandates `Path=/`). The edge cache-skip check and the audience bucketing were updated to recognize the prefixed names so a signed-in response is never served from the shared edge cache.
